model.rationale: Kennedy combines a D+11 district, incumbency, and a roughly 500-to-1 fundraising advantage over Hannon, while markets price his win odds near 97 percent. With no polling suggesting competition, the race sits firmly in Safe D territory.
model.watch: A late surge of outside spending for Hannon or an unexpected controversy involving Kennedy would be the main ways this race could tighten.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.

overview:
NY-26 sits in the Buffalo area and leans Democratic by about eleven points on partisanship alone. Tim Kennedy, the Democratic incumbent, is running for re-election, and no public general-election polls or expert ratings are available for this race. What evidence exists points strongly toward Kennedy: prediction markets price his chances near 97 percent, and his campaign has built a large financial edge.

Kennedy has raised roughly $2.8 million and holds about $1.2 million on hand, while Republican Dennis Hannon has reported about $5,500 raised and under $5,000 in cash. That gap, roughly five hundred to one, leaves Hannon little ability to introduce himself or advertise in a district already tilted against his party. The forecast expects Kennedy to win comfortably, with the main uncertainty coming from the absence of polling rather than any sign of a competitive race.
